questions.stem: Q1. A 53-year-old man presents to his primary care physician with complaints of feeling like the room is spinning, dizziness, decreased hearing, ringing in the ears, and fullness in both ears. He states that the symptoms have been occurring episodically but increasing in frequency. The ringing in his ears was not present initially but has become more prominent. He denies any recent ear infections or trauma. He is not taking any medications. On examination, he is noted to have low-frequency hearing loss. The remainder of the examination is normal. After a complete workup is done, the patient is diagnosed with Ménière disease. What part of the vestibular system detects angular acceleration and rotation?

questions.stem: Q1. A 44-year-old woman presents to her gynecologist with complaints of not having a period for the last 8 months. She reports a negative pregnancy test at home. Upon further questioning, she reports a daily headache, changes in vision, and a milky discharge from the breast. She has no medical problems and is not taking any medications. questions.stem: Q1. A 19-year-old woman with a history of diplopia and paresthesia is diagnosed with multiple sclerosis (MS). The explanation often cited for this effect is that cold increases the duration of the action potential. Which of the following best explains why increasing the duration of the action potential can restore nerve conduction in patients with MS?
questions.stemHtml: Q1. A 19-year-old woman with a history of diplopia and paresthesia is diagnosed with multiple sclerosis (MS). options.label: A

options.label: D
options.text: The amount of sodium entering the nerve with each action potential increases.
